title: Three-copy undistillability of the Werner endpoint
statement: For every integer d >= 3, is rho = (I - F/2)/(d^2 - d/2) three-copy undistillable, where F swaps the two C^d factors? Equivalently, is <psi|(rho^Gamma)^(tensor 3)|psi> >= 0 for every unit vector psi of Schmidt rank at most two across A1A2A3:B1B2B3, with Gamma the partial transpose on B?
source_locator: Wu and Zou, Section 1.1, equations (1)-(3); Fu, Gao and Park, Section 4; Zenodo candidate description.
status_basis: The primary sources leave the unrestricted three-copy question open. A later unreviewed d=3 candidate is retained as a claim, not an established answer. The scoped search found no resolution covering all d >= 3.
plain_summary: Can three copies unlock entanglement distillation that a single copy cannot achieve? This finite-copy question probes the limits of entanglement as a communication resource.
assumptions: Finite-dimensional complex spaces, d >= 3, and local operations and classical communication (LOCC).
The bipartition groups all Alice copies against all Bob copies; it is not a three-party problem.
The endpoint is alpha = -1/2. A coefficient operator need not be Hermitian, positive or normal.

Under vectorization psi=vec(C), Schmidt rank equals rank(C). The equivalent homogeneous test is q_3(C)=||C||_HS^2 -(1/2) sum_i ||Tr_i C||_HS^2 +(1/4) sum_i<j ||Tr_ij C||_HS^2 -(1/8)|Tr C|^2 >= 0 for every complex rank-at-most-two C on (C^d) tensor 3. Partial traces are unnormalized; their subscripts name the factors removed.
scope: The target quantifies over every d >= 3. A d=4 study is Curator-proposed; pending review. Its novelty requires a separate check, and a positive answer there is only partial progress.
target: Prove the displayed nonnegativity for the full domain, or exhibit one admissible vector giving a rigorously negative value.
success_criteria: A positive result must cover every permitted Schmidt-rank-two vector and every dimension claimed.
A negative result must retain exact vector or coefficient data, rank justification and certified strict negativity.
State precisely which dimensions or subclasses remain untreated.
known_results: Wu and Zou report nonnegativity for positive semidefinite and normal rank-two coefficient operators and specified nonnormal support configurations.
Fu, Gao and Park report the exact two-copy threshold; their theorem does not settle three or arbitrarily many copies.
The anonymous d=3 deposit is a candidate claim whose certificate has not been inspected here.
prerequisites: Partial transpose, Schmidt rank, LOCC and matrix inequalities.
Tensor indices, unnormalized partial traces and certified arithmetic.
significance: The full target is a concrete step toward understanding NPT entanglement. Its significance is foundational; no immediate communications-hardware improvement follows.

relations.explanation: Tests one finite-copy layer of the Werner route to NPT bound entanglement. Neither a three-copy positivity theorem nor a distillation witness for this family settles the unrestricted all-copy existence question.
The two-copy boundary is a reported recent advance, retained separately with its unresolved independent-review requirements.
